script.text: Blood cells from an eighty year old now read as under twenty. How?

Researchers at the University of Bonn report in the journal Aging Cell that they turned red blood cell precursors from an eighty year old donor directly into neural stem cells. They skipped the usual detour through stem cells that can become anything.

Then they checked age with epigenetic clocks. These read chemical tags on D.N.A. that build up over a lifetime. By that measure, the new cells came out younger than twenty. The team says it was unplanned. The change unfolded slowly.

The paper was peer reviewed. This is still a laboratory result in cells in a dish, not a treatment for people. Epigenetic clocks are a proxy for biological age. The lead researcher says the cells also behave like young cells. That claim comes from the authors.
Will cell rejuvenation ever reach patients? Yes or no?
